The page covers the ALLPOWERS R4000 power station only. It doesn't recommend a specific solar panel, so it isn't really a "combo" page.

**The deal**
- Store price is $1,499 (the list price of $3,299 is a markup, so ignore it).
- Code **EXTRA12** takes 12% off orders over $1,200, which brings it to **$1,319.12**. It expires 2026-11-15. The site says it tested the code in ALLPOWERS's cart on 2026-10-23.
- Other codes are weaker. ALLPOWERS26 and EXTRA10 each give $1,349.10. The store usually allows one code per order, so use EXTRA12.
- Buy here (affiliate link, no extra cost to you): [ALLPOWERS R4000 at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). Check the final price at checkout.

**Specs**
- Capacity is 3,456 Wh, LiFePO4, rated for 3,500+ cycles. The warranty is 5 years.
- AC output is 3,600 W continuous at 120 V, with 6,000 W peak. The "4,000 W" in the name is the 230 V rating, not what you get in the US.
- Solar input is up to 2,000 W across 3 XT60 inputs, at 650 W each and 12–60 V. You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W.
- AC recharge takes about 2 hours.
- It has an RV outlet, and it weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb).

**For an RV**
- It's a good fit if you want to run an AC unit, microwave or induction cooktop. It has plenty of capacity and a dedicated RV outlet.
- At 45 kg, it's a unit you set in place, not one you carry around.
- Returns are 30 days for unused items, and you pay return shipping. The refund page also says sale items can't be returned, so check whether this purchase counts as a sale item.
- The site earns a commission on purchases through its link.

**Solar panels**
The page names none. The R4000 accepts up to 650 W per input, so you could use something like 2–3 high-voltage panels per input, staying within 12–60 V. Check the voltage rating before you buy any panel.

I can look at specific panels that fit those input limits, for either a roof-mounted or a portable setup, if you'd like. Tell me roughly how much roof space you have and how much you want to spend.
